seoTitle: How to Permanently Delete Your Namecheap Account
metaDescription: Ready to close your Namecheap account for good? Learn the exact steps to log in, request account deletion, and confirm the permanent cancellation.
intro: Whether you're switching to another registrar or simply cleaning up unused accounts, permanently deleting a Namecheap account requires going through account settings rather than just letting it sit idle. This guide walks through logging in, finding the account-level settings where deletion lives, and what to sort out with your active services before you request it, so the process goes through cleanly on the first try.

steps.heading: Log in to your Namecheap account
steps.body: Head to Namecheap's login page and sign in with your username and password. If you're not signed in yet, the same page offers account creation on the right, but for a deletion you'll obviously be using the Log In panel on the left. The Domains menu at the top gives quick access to domain-related tools like TLD List and Whois Lookup, but none of that is where account deletion lives — it's tucked into your profile settings instead, which you'll only see after logging in.

image.caption: Namecheap's login page, with the Domains menu open showing tools like Domain Transfer and TLD List that sit separately from account settings.

steps.heading: Review what's active on your account first
steps.body: Once logged in, the Dashboard lists everything Recently Active in Your Account — each domain, its associated products (hosting icons, email icons), and its expiration date, with a Manage button next to each one. Before requesting deletion, it's worth scanning this list closely: any domain, hosting plan, SSL certificate, or privacy protection service still active here needs to be handled — cancelled, transferred out, or allowed to lapse — because an account with live services attached is far more likely to hit friction during closure than an account with nothing left running.

image.caption: The Namecheap Dashboard, listing active domains with their products and expiration dates — the starting point for checking what needs to be cancelled first.

steps.heading: Cancel or transfer active services
steps.body: For any domain you want to keep, either transfer it to another registrar (which requires unlocking it and grabbing its EPP/Auth code beforehand) or simply let it run out its term elsewhere before deletion. For hosting, SSL certificates, or privacy protection you no longer need, cancel each one individually from its respective management page rather than assuming account deletion will clean them up automatically — Namecheap treats deletion and service cancellation as separate actions.

steps.heading: Open your profile settings
steps.body: With services squared away, click your username in the top right and open Profile from the account menu. This is where Namecheap groups account-level settings that aren't tied to any single domain or product — personal details, password, two-factor authentication, and the security options that eventually lead to account closure.

steps.heading: Go to the Security section and find Account Deletion
steps.body: Inside Profile, open the Security tab. Account-level security settings and the deletion request option live together here, separate from anything domain-specific. Look for the Account Deletion option specifically — it's a distinct action from simply removing a payment method or disabling two-factor authentication, both of which are also managed from this same area but don't touch the account's existence.

steps.heading: Confirm the deletion request
steps.body: Selecting Account Deletion starts a confirmation flow, typically requiring you to verify your identity or confirm the request through your email before it's finalized. Read whatever warning Namecheap shows at this stage carefully — permanent deletion is meant to be final, and it will flag if you still have active domains or balances attached that need resolving first. Once confirmed, the account closure processes and you should no longer be able to log in with those credentials afterward.

faq.question: Can I delete my Namecheap account if I still have active domains?
faq.answer: Active domains or services can complicate deletion, so it's best to transfer them out or let them expire before requesting account closure.

faq.question: Is deleting a Namecheap account reversible?
faq.answer: No, permanent deletion is meant to be final, so make sure you no longer need the account before confirming.

faq.question: Will deleting my account remove my domain registrations too?
faq.answer: Domains typically need to be transferred or expired separately, since account deletion doesn't automatically remove active domain registrations.

faq.question: Where exactly is the account deletion option?
faq.answer: It's under your username menu → Profile → Security, grouped with other account-level security settings rather than under any specific domain or product.

faq.question: How long does the deletion process take?
faq.answer: It varies, but the request and confirmation steps are generally completed within the same session once initiated, provided no active services are blocking it.
